requirement:
When preparing the mandatory input set defined by
{cite}`requirements.authoring.mandatory_inputs`, every terminology definition
referenced by the subject or any contributed source MUST contribute its complete
fenced declaration, including its phrase option. Definitions referenced by those
definitions MUST also be included transitively, without duplicates or
nontermination on cycles.

When an additional source read introduces a terminology dependency, the same
complete, transitive definition set MUST be supplied to the model and recorded
before accepting a submission.
rationale:
**Judgment:** the implementation and tests satisfy `requirements.definitions.authoring_inputs`. The remaining gaps are minor and none is acknowledged by a FIXME.

**Implementation**

- **Mandatory set (`AssessmentSources::prepare`, `src/authoring/inputs.rs`).**
  - It builds the contributed inputs: the subject, its `{cite}`d requirements, the `{impl}`/`{test}` outline selectors, and the anchors.
  - It then calls `definition_inputs(..., &mandatory, Some(&subject.text))`. That call scans the subject text and every contributed input for term references.
  - New definitions are appended with `!mandatory.contains(..)`, so the set has no duplicates.
- **Transitive closure (`terms::dependencies`, `src/terms.rs`).**
  - `direct_references` collects term roles from the subject text.
  - Requirements inputs are scanned in their declaration bodies.
  - Rust outline inputs are scanned in comments only.
  - Other outline inputs are scanned as whole text.
  - Definition inputs add themselves.
  - `close_dependencies` is a worklist with a `visited` set. It expands each definition's body to a fixed point, so there are no duplicates and cycles terminate.
- **Complete declaration (`InputSelector::resolve`, `src/inputs.rs`).** For a Definition selector it returns `target.raw_lines`, the whole fenced declaration including the `:phrase:` line. `source_input` also applies access checks.
- **Additional reads (`tools::read`, `tools::search`, `additional_definitions`).**
  - Every `habeas` read form (line range, item, requirements, definition) and `ripgrep` computes the closure over the delivered inputs. It returns the definitions in the tool result (`definitions` field), so the model is supplied with them.
  - `additional_definitions` drops definitions already delivered or already recorded.
  - `read` and `search` also append the definitions to `ToolDelivery.inputs`.
- **Recording before acceptance (`converse`, `src/authoring/mod.rs`).** `pending` holds the mandatory inputs and each tool's delivered inputs, including definitions. `record_inputs(&pending)` runs after every successful provider response and before the submission is parsed. Definitions introduced by a read are therefore recorded before a submission is accepted. Built-ins are supplied but not recorded, as intended.
- **Marking.** The code that does this work carries `{impl}` references to the requirement: `prepare`, `record_inputs`, `additional_definitions`, `source_input`, `definition_inputs`, `converse`, `read` and `search`.
  - `prepare_citation` also calls `definition_inputs` without its own `{impl}`. It is a different assessment kind and reuses the marked helper, so I did not count this as a gap.

**Tests**

- **Mandatory bundle (`bundle_combines_direct_references_terms_and_current_existing_selectors`).**
  - Terms `unit` and `value` reference each other, forming a cycle. The subject references only `unit`.
  - The test asserts exactly two definition inputs: both are present, once each, and the cycle terminates.
  - It also checks the exclusion of the unrelated `distant` requirement.
- **Staging (`mandatory_git_inputs_require_staging_declarations_sources_and_terms`).** An unstaged term declaration aborts preparation, and the term is supplied once it is staged.
- **Introduced by a read (`definitions_introduced_by_a_read_are_supplied_and_recorded_before_submission`).**
  - A read of a source whose comment references `value` also pulls in `unit` transitively. The cycle is present again.
  - The test asserts that the recorded definitions are exactly `[terms.unit, terms.value]`, once each, and that each starts with `:::{definition}` followed by `:phrase:`.
  - It also asserts that the second request, but not the first, contains the transitive text, and that the submission came after delivery.
- **Tool tests.** `reading_records_only_delivered_sources_and_their_terms` and `search_supplies_terminology_clamps_at_eof_and_reports_failures` check that definitions appear in the tool results and are recorded, with no duplicates after repeated recording.

**Minor gaps, not enough to fail**

- No test has a cited requirement, rather than the subject or a source, carry the term reference.
- No test has a term already in the mandatory set that a later read would re-reference.
- Both paths use the same deduplicating helpers, so I judged the risk low.

text: :::{req} authoring_inputs
When preparing the mandatory input set defined by
{cite}`requirements.authoring.mandatory_inputs`, every terminology definition
referenced by the subject or any contributed source MUST contribute its complete
fenced declaration, including its phrase option. Definitions referenced by those
definitions MUST also be included transitively, without duplicates or
nontermination on cycles.
When an additional source read introduces a terminology dependency, the same
complete, transitive definition set MUST be supplied to the model and recorded
before accepting a submission.
:::{req} mandatory_inputs
The harness MUST construct each assessment's mandatory input set by combining
the contributions specified by the requirements applicable to that subject and
its inputs. A requirement that contributes inputs MUST cite this requirement and
define which sources it contributes and when. The harness MUST include every
applicable contribution, deduplicate identical selections, and report
unresolvable mandatory inputs before inference. The complete set MUST be supplied
in the initial model request.
Generated output under project-root `evidence/`, including symlink aliases, MUST
be omitted from mandatory inputs when the default exclusion applies. An explicit
workspace allow MUST permit those selections; an explicit disallow MUST abort
under {cite}`requirements.authoring.read_denial`.
